name: ROUND
desc: Covers decimal rounding of numbers and strings: current-node and explicit operands, all six modes by name and ID, at and shift, NUM/INT/STR/SIG output, decimal carries, signed zero in strings, significant precision, scientific notation and large logical magnitudes, value-context options, namespaces, match error trapping, guarded evaluation, and invalid syntax and operands. Numeric expectations use small integers or exact binary fractions. Host-specific numeric storage limits, nonfinite extensions, and numeric negative-zero preservation are not prescribed.

tests.name: Defaults and operand forms
tests.desc: The first operand is always options, including the integer shorthand for shift. Omitted input means the current node; explicit input does not inspect the type of that node. Numbers default to NUM and strings default to STR.

Rounding modes
tests.desc: Each row tests below-half, exact-half with even and odd retained digits, above-half, negative counterparts, and an exact integer. The same matrix is required for each mode name and numeric ID. String inputs avoid binary floating-point and signed-zero decoder differences.

Decimal positions, shifts, and carries
tests.desc: at chooses a decimal position without rescaling the result; shift changes the value before rounding. Point movement and scientific exponents use decimal arithmetic. Exact ties and digits beyond the first discarded digit must be distinguished.

Output formats and result types
tests.desc: All output formats accept numeric IDs or uppercase names. STR is pure decimal with exactly max(at, 0) fractional digits. NUM and INT return numbers even from string inputs. INT checks the final rounded value for an exact integer rather than rejecting fractional input or positive at in advance.

tests.name: INT permits positive at when result is integral
Significant decimal precision
tests.desc: SIG keeps the lesser of the input precision after shift and the requested rounding position. Trailing whole-number zeroes are not significant; trailing fractional zeroes are. These cases include all examples from the ROUND specification, plus decimal padding avoidance, carries, shifted precision, negative values, and zero.

Signed zero in string output
tests.desc: A string supplies a known sign even when its value is zero. STR and SIG can preserve that sign. Numeric signed zero is not required because host input decoders and numeric storage may discard it.

tests.name: Negative zero is not rounded away
Value contexts and namespaces
tests.desc: Options and explicit input are evaluated in value context. Option-object property values are expressions too. Reused common expressions resolve the invoking node and bindings each time.

tests.name: Common expression uses invoking TEMP options
Invalid input types
tests.desc: Only numbers and strings are valid input types. Referenced arrays remain data, even when their contents resemble expression notation. A known literal error outside a match may be rejected statically.

tests.name: Date is not a number or string
CASTNUM string syntax extensions
tests.desc: String input follows CASTNUM syntax, including a leading plus sign and a trailing decimal point. STR output omits a positive sign and uses the precision requested by at.

tests.name: Leading plus and trailing decimal point
Negative zero with trailing decimal point
Invalid decimal text
tests.desc: Non-numeric strings are invalid targets rather than options errors. String input follows CASTNUM syntax, without surrounding whitespace. A sign or decimal point alone does not supply a number.

tests.name: Invalid options
tests.desc: The options operand must be an integer shift or an object. mode and as accept only listed names or IDs; at and shift require integer numbers. Computed values retain INVALID_OPERAND classification, with INVALID_GRAFT also permitted for intrinsically invalid literal parameters.

tests.name: Evaluation failures and matching
tests.desc: Errors from evaluating operands propagate from value context. Match probes trap INVALID_TARGET and runtime INVALID_OPERAND, including when an ANY alternative recovers. Invalid syntax and recursive resource exhaustion remain fatal.
